scope_note: Verdicts cover the changed units listed in t003-rev51/changed-units.txt. Skipped: the [NOCHECK] status lines L3 and L4; L133 and L134 (context only); page.yaml (no strings changed). The L188 [LABEL] is checked even though its line ends in <!-- nocheck -->, because the change list names it as a checkable [LABEL] unit, not [NOCHECK]. Every evidence span and every quote in the changed sentences was string-matched against passages.md. Each unit carries an extra 'reason' field because the brief asks for a reason with every tag verdict.

units.sentence: Who it affects: Fulton County residents and property owners.
units.marker: {analysis: the budget pays for county services residents use (P-054, P-103), and property owners pay the property tax (P-101, P-102)}
units.reason: P-054 lists the services the General Fund pays for, and P-103 says the budget reflects 'the needs of our residents'. P-101 makes property tax the main revenue, and P-102 ties the bill to property value and millage rate, so 'property owners pay' follows directly. The sentence doesn't claim to be a complete list.

units.sentence: Property tax is the county's main income.
units.evidence_span: The County’s primary source of revenue is property tax.
units.reason: 'Main income' is a plain rendering of 'primary source of revenue'.

units.sentence: Whether your 2027 county property tax changes isn't known as of Nov 8, 2026; the proposal wasn't posted, and the tax rate is decided separately.
units.marker: {analysis: no 2027 proposal was on the county's budget page on Nov 8 (P-045); in the 2026 cycle, the tax rate (millage rate) was a separate decision, planned for after the January budget vote (P-046, P-098, P-101)}
units.reason: P-045 (captured Nov 8) lists only FY2026 documents. P-101 shows the FY2026 budget assumed the rate set 'when setting the FY2025 millage rate', with the FY2026 rate to be set in summer 2026. P-098 is the Sept 30, 2026 rate hearing, after the Jan 21 budget vote (P-046). So two cycles show the rate decided separately from the budget.
units.problem: Minor (no change required): 'the tax rate is decided separately' is a present-tense statement about 2027 that rests on past practice (FY2025 and FY2026). No passage says how the 2027 rate will be set. The tag discloses the basis, and the line's last sentence gives the 2026 example.
units.suggested_fix: Optional: '...the proposal wasn't posted, and in 2026 the tax rate was decided separately.'

units.sentence: In 2026, a tax-rate hearing was set for Sept 30, after January's budget vote.
units.evidence_span: will convene a Special Called Meeting on Wednesday, September 30, 2026 at 10 a.m. in the Fulton County Government Center, 141 Pryor Street, SW, Atlanta, Georgia 30303 for the purpose of a Public Hearing on proposed millage rate
units.reason: P-046 dates the budget approval to January 21, 2026. 'Was set for' correctly doesn't claim the hearing took place.

units.sentence: What the jail, courts, prosecutors and public defense get for 2027 isn't known as of Nov 8, 2026.
units.marker: {analysis: the budget page on Nov 8 had no 2027 proposal (P-045)}
units.reason: P-045, captured Nov 8, 2026, lists only FY2026 documents.
units.problem: Wording only: see the framing issue on 'public defense' (undefined here, and less familiar than 'public defender').

units.sentence: The archived text of the Clerk's web page doesn't say where to submit comments or requests.
units.marker: {analysis: P-067 is the public-comment text we archived from that page}
units.reason: P-067 says comments and requests 'must be submitted before the clerk sounds the start of the 10 a.m. meeting' but gives no place, link or form. The other S11 excerpts (P-097, P-099, P-100) don't either. Scoping the claim to 'archived text' is accurate.
units.problem: Minor: as a negative claim about the whole archived page, it can be checked here only against the S11 excerpts, not the full snapshot.

units.sentence: The public defender's office defends people who can't afford a lawyer.
units.reason: No passage defines the office, so the {analysis} tag is correct. The definition is accurate in plain language.
units.problem: Minor accuracy: slightly broader than the office's role. A public defender represents people charged with crimes, not people in civil matters such as evictions. The same wording is at L143 and L166.
units.suggested_fix: The public defender's office defends people charged with crimes who can't afford a lawyer.

units.sentence: The county manager carries out the budget once the Board adopts it.
units.evidence_span: The county manager is authorized to take all administrative steps necessary to implement the budget as approved.
units.reason: 'Carries out' renders 'implement', and 'once the Board adopts it' renders 'as approved'. A fair plain-language reading.

units.sentence: The district attorney prosecutes serious crimes, called felonies.
units.reason: No passage defines the office, so the tag is correct. Accurate: the district attorney handles felony prosecution, and the solicitor-general (defined in the same line) handles misdemeanors.
units.problem: See the framing issue: 'misdemeanors', in the unchanged solicitor-general sentence earlier on the line, is still undefined.

units.sentence: The court clerk keeps court records.
units.marker: {analysis: plain-language definition; P-054 names the office "Superior & Magistrate Court - Clerk"}
units.reason: No passage states the clerk's duties, so the tag is correct. The quoted office name appears verbatim in P-054. Accurate plain language, though not a complete list of duties.

units.sentence: The county manager carries out the budget once the Board adopts it.
units.evidence_span: The county manager is authorized to take all administrative steps necessary to implement the budget as approved.
units.reason: Same as L64.

units.sentence: Resolution 26-0729 would have added to the code: "No limits or caps shall be placed on what a department, agency, elected official, or authority can request."
units.evidence_span: No limits or caps shall be placed on what a department, agency, elected official, or authority can request.
units.reason: The quote is verbatim. The sentence is in the proposed Sec. 2-261 (P-030) but absent from the as-adopted text (P-005), and the passage note marks it as underlined (new). 'Would have' fits the 'Filed' status in P-024.

units.sentence: It says the change would "clarify that all departmental budget requests are included in the proposed budget."
units.evidence_span: amends F.C.C. Sec. 2-261 to clarify that all departmental budget requests are included in the proposed budget
units.reason: Verbatim, except the original continues 'as follows:'. The words are attributed to the resolution, not to Barrett, and 'It' clearly refers to Resolution 26-0729.

units.sentence: The Fulton County Board of Commissioners, a chairman and six district seats, must adopt a budget by its second regular January meeting.
units.evidence_span: The budget shall then be adopted by the board of commissioners by no later than the second regular meeting in January of the year to which it applies
units.reason: P-035 lists 'Chairman (At-Large)' and Districts 1 to 6, with District 4 vacant, so 'six district seats' is accurate.

units.sentence: Option C, a proposal to change how drafts are built, was filed (set aside) on Nov 4.
units.evidence_span: to require that all departmental budget requests are disclosed in the proposed budget; and for other purposes. (Barrett) (MOTION TO APPROVE FAILED ON 10/21/26) (FILED)
units.reason: P-024 and P-025 support 'filed on Nov 4': status 'Filed', and a substitute motion 'to file' passed on 2026-11-04. P-024's title supports 'a proposal to change how drafts are built'.
units.problem: Low. '(set aside)' is a plain-language definition that no passage gives, and it now sits untagged inside a [P-###] sentence. It came from folding in the separate sentence 'Filing set Option C aside without approving it.', and the fold lost that sentence's own tag and the words 'without approving it' (compare L81, where the same gloss is tagged {analysis}). The same untagged gloss appears in unchanged text: L121's third sentence, L172, home.md L14 and the page.yaml chip 'Set aside (filed) Nov 4'. If the project treats 'filed, or set aside' as an accepted reading of P-024/P-025, close this with no change.
units.suggested_fix: Keep 60 words by making the sentence an analysis unit: 'Option C, a proposal to change how drafts are built, was set aside (filed) on Nov 4. {analysis: status "Filed" after a Nov 4 vote to file, with no later step (P-024, P-025)}'

units.sentence: If you care most about early, balanced Board input: Resolution 26-0460, which Commissioner Bob Ellis sponsored, says today's Budget Commission adds "earlier and ongoing input from members of the Board," with north-south "balanced representation."
units.evidence_span: earlier and ongoing input from members of the Board, structured to ensure balanced representation from both the northern and southern portions of Fulton County
units.reason: Both quotes are verbatim in P-004, and 'adds' fairly paraphrases 'combines ... with'. The words are attributed to the resolution, not to Ellis personally. The sponsor is supported by P-016 ('SPONSORED BY: Bob Ellis') and P-017 ('(Ellis/Abdur-Rahman)').
units.problem: Minor (see framing issues): names only Ellis, though P-016/P-017 list Vice Chair Abdur-Rahman as co-sponsor. Accurate but incomplete.

units.sentence: Both sides claim transparency: Option C aims "to ensure transparency," and Commissioner Ellis said today's process is "more transparent and open" than in recent years.
units.marker: {analysis: Option C's aim is in its title (P-024, P-032); Ellis's statement is P-073, a comparison card 4 rates Uncertain}
units.reason: 'to ensure transparency' is verbatim in P-024's title. 'more transparent and open' is verbatim in P-073 ('...than anything we’ve had in recent years'), and the paraphrase keeps the sense. The colon makes clear which two sides are meant, and each side gets the same verb ('claim') with no extra caveat.
units.problem: Minor citation precision: P-032 is the sponsor line, not the title. P-024 (or P-027) holds the title, and the sentence doesn't name Barrett.
units.suggested_fix: Optional: cite '(P-024, P-027)' for the title.

units.sentence: No archived source argues for Option A over Option B, or the reverse.
units.marker: {analysis: no archived statement argues for adopting the proposal unchanged or for changing it; both options keep today's process}
units.reason: No passage argues for adopting the unpublished proposal unchanged or for amending it. The officials ask about timing and more funding (P-070, P-071, P-077). Ellis's statements (P-073, P-079) and P-028's 'make adjustments' clause are about process, not Option A versus B. The change from {editorial} to {analysis} is right, because this is a checkable claim about the archive.

units.sentence: No source we archived gives a reason for the 5% limit, so no line speaks for it.
units.marker: {analysis: the minutes record votes only (P-088, P-092); see "Not known yet"}
units.reason: Every passage that mentions the cap (P-024, P-027, P-029, P-031, P-037, P-077, P-088, P-092) describes or opposes it, and none gives the commission's reason. Ellis's statements (P-073, P-079) don't mention the limit. Leaving out a line for the limit, rather than writing an anticipated argument, follows invariants 4 and 5.
units.problem: Minor: the tag cites only the minutes, but the claim covers every archived source. It holds for all passages; the full snapshots behind the excerpted news passages can't be checked from passages.md.

units.sentence: The 2026 plan left savings about $2.8 million above the least the county must keep.
units.marker: {computed: $179,000,901 − $176,218,666 = $2,782,235, from P-054's "Fund Balance Minimum Reserve Requirement"}
units.reason: Recomputed: 179,000,901 − 176,218,666 = 2,782,235, which rounds to $2.8 million. Both figures are from P-054's 2026 Adopted column. The source's own 252,638,514 − 73,637,614 = 179,000,900 is $1 off, a rounding in the source that doesn't affect the result.
units.problem: Two minor points. (1) Tense: 'left' can read as an actual year-end result, but $179,000,901 is the adopted plan's projected ending balance and 2026 hadn't closed. L108 and L242 say 'leaves'. (2) The quoted row name 'Fund Balance Minimum Reserve Requirement' isn't a contiguous string in P-054, where the label wraps around the figures ('Fund Balance Minimum Reserve $ 139,628,982 ... $ 176,218,666 Requirement'). An exact-match quote check would miss it.
units.suggested_fix: 'The 2026 plan leaves savings about $2.8 million above the least the county must keep.' In the tag, quote 'Fund Balance Minimum Reserve' or write the row name without quotation marks.

units.sentence: Resolution 26-0729 and FOX 5 say that limit holds requests for extra money to 5% of current funding.
units.evidence_span: limit any request for additional funding to 5% above current allocations
units.reason: Both sources support 'requests for extra money' (P-029: 'the 5% cap on departmental enhancement requests'; P-077: 'any request for additional funding'). FOX 5 supports '5% of current funding'.
units.problem: Low. The sentence credits '5% of current funding' to both sources, but only FOX 5 says it ('5% above current allocations'). The resolution measures the cap against each department's 'base budget' for 2027 (P-029: 'requests that do not exceed 5% of their “base budget” for 2027'). The passages define 'Base Budget' only for 2026 (P-086, not cited here), and L119, L122 and card 3 keep the two terms apart. The 30-second tag (L8) also credits 'current allocations' to P-077 alone. The same merged wording is in unchanged L92 and L166.
units.suggested_fix: 'FOX 5 says that limit holds requests for extra money to 5% above current funding; Resolution 26-0729 measures it against each department's "base budget."' [P-077, P-080, P-029, P-024]

units.reason: No passage gives it, so the tag is correct. Accurate plain language.

units.problem: Minor accuracy, as at L51: slightly broader than the office's role, which covers people charged with crimes.

units.sentence: If the Board adds money, the offices it funds, and the people who use their services, gain.
units.reason: P-047 lets the Board adopt sums 'greater or less than the sums presented in the proposed budget'. The conditional benefit is a fair inference. The split didn't change the meaning, and 'it' in 'the offices it funds' clearly means the Board.

units.sentence: If the Board cuts, taxpayers and the county's savings gain.
units.reason: A fair conditional inference that mirrors Option A's 'Who benefits' (L142). The 2026 plan drew on savings (P-054).

units.sentence: If the Board adds money, taxpayers, other programs or savings pay.
units.reason: A fair inference: added spending must come from revenue, other lines or fund balance (compare P-006's financing rule for increases, and the 2026 use of fund balance in P-054). Symmetric with L150.

units.sentence: If the Board cuts, the offices cut, and the people who use their services, pay.
units.reason: A fair conditional inference, symmetric with L150.

units.sentence: The Fulton County Board of Commissioners, a chairman and six district seats, adopts the budget.
units.evidence_span: Final authority to adopt the annual budget remains exclusively with the full board of commissioners
units.reason: P-035 gives the chairman (At-Large) and six district seats.

units.sentence: The Board's votes are listed under What happened, on the Summary tab.
units.reason: What happened (L76 to L81) gives the roll calls from P-020 (Aug 5), P-023 (Aug 19), P-033 (Oct 21) and P-034 (Nov 4).
units.problem: Can't be checked from the allowed files: whether that section renders on a tab named 'Summary', since the renderer is out of scope. It fits the brief's note that L16 and L51 are on the same tab.

units.sentence: Atlanta News First said it was still waiting to hear back from the vice chair, who serves on the commission.
units.evidence_span: Atlanta News First is still waiting to hear back from Commissioner Khadijah Abdur-Rahman.

In its new place it follows the sentence naming Vice Chair Abdur-Rahman, so 'the vice chair' is clear, and it explains why only Ellis is quoted for that side.

units.sentence: The sources quote Chief Probate Judge Kenya Johnson, Sheriff Patrick Labat and Commissioner Dana Barrett criticizing the process, plus Solicitor-General Keith Gammage on funding.
units.reason: P-078 quotes Johnson and Labat criticizing the process, P-072 quotes Barrett, and P-071 and P-077 quote Gammage on underfunding and 'a lack of proper investment'. 'The sources' (was 'They') now has a clear referent, and the verbs match the other side ('backing' and 'criticizing').

units.sentence: The district attorney and solicitor-general prosecute crimes.
units.reason: Same as L143: correctly tagged and accurate.

units.reason: Same as L143: correctly tagged and accurate.

units.sentence: The public defender's office defends people who can't afford a lawyer.
units.reason: Same as L143: correctly tagged and accurate in plain language.
units.problem: Minor accuracy, as at L51: covers people charged with crimes, not all legal matters.
units.suggested_fix: The public defender's office defends people charged with crimes who can't afford a lawyer.

units.sentence: Card 2 evidence label: "Hearings scheduled as commission meetings: Supported (county notice)"
units.marker: evidence label, no [P-###]; 'county notice' is P-042, which the card cites at L192
units.evidence_span: Special called meetings of the Fulton County Budget Commission will be conducted on the dates and locations provided above for the purpose of holding budget hearings
units.reason: The notice schedules the hearings as the commission's special called meetings. Changing 'held' to 'scheduled' removes the earlier implication that they took place, which the notice can't show.

units.sentence: Ellis's archived statements don't address the eligibility rules.
units.marker: {analysis: P-073 and P-079 are his archived statements}
units.reason: P-073 (open meetings, committee structure, 'more transparent', no early vote) and P-079 (the commission drafts recommendations and the full Board votes) are the only passages quoting or paraphrasing Ellis. Neither mentions eligibility, term or tenure, or Barrett's 'only they qualify', even though ANF frames P-073 as his response to her allegation. Card 4 has a parallel gap note for the other side (L217), so the treatment is even.

units.sentence: If the claim is right, the commission holds "open meetings," and "all commissioners and their staff are able to attend and hear what is said," in Commissioner Bob Ellis's words.
units.evidence_span: Those meetings are open meetings. They are speaking and addressing the budget commission just like a standard committee structure, but all commissioners and their staff are able to attend and hear what is said
units.reason: Both quotes are verbatim and keep their sense. 'Open meetings' refers to the commission's meetings, and the second quote, as written, is about commissioners and staff rather than the public. 'If the claim is right' mirrors card 3's In short on the other side.

units.sentence: Records back the announced hearings, not the past-years comparison.
units.marker: {analysis: P-042 and P-055 to P-058; the comparison is Ellis's, in P-073}
units.reason: P-042 is the county's public notice of the six hearings, and P-055 to P-058 show the posted slides. No passage tests Ellis's claim that the process is 'more transparent and open than anything we’ve had in recent years'. 'Announced' correctly doesn't claim the hearings took place or were open.

units.sentence: The message said the volume of requests and known budget pressures "resulted in many unmet requests."
units.evidence_span: The volume of requests coupled with known budget pressures and financial resources resulted in many unmet requests.
units.reason: The quote is verbatim. The paraphrase drops 'and financial resources' from the causes without changing the sense. P-046 ties the message to the FY2026 proposal.

units.sentence: When that proposal was written, consent decree costs were "still being vetted and have not been determined," though the county expected them to grow.
units.evidence_span: all decree compliance related costs are still being vetted and have not been determined, but as costs accelerate from partial year to full year recurring implementation, this number is expected to grow
units.reason: The quote is verbatim, and 'expected them to grow' matches 'this number is expected to grow'. 'When that proposal was written' correctly dates the message's 'To date' instead of presenting it as current.
units.problem: Minor: P-050 alone doesn't show that the text is from the message sent with the proposal. P-046 does, and it is cited on the two sentences before. See the framing issue on 'that proposal'.

units.sentence: That leaves savings about $2.8 million above the least the county must keep.
units.marker: {computed: $179,000,901 − $176,218,666 = $2,782,235, from P-054's "Fund Balance Minimum Reserve Requirement"}
units.reason: Recomputed: 2,782,235, about $2.8 million, from P-054's 2026 Adopted column. Present-tense 'leaves', following 'The 2026 plan spends...', correctly treats it as a plan figure.
units.problem: Minor: the same tag-quote issue as L142. 'Fund Balance Minimum Reserve Requirement' is split by figures in P-054.
units.suggested_fix: Quote 'Fund Balance Minimum Reserve', or write the row name without quotation marks.

units.sentence: Speak at the Fulton County Board of Commissioners' public comment, in person or by Zoom, before it adopts the budget.
units.evidence_span: Residents have two options to participate in public comment: in person and virtually via Zoom.
units.reason: The cited passages support each part except the timing. P-039 gives the Nov 18, 10 a.m. regular meeting. P-036 provides public comment at first and second regular meetings, before the business portion. P-067 gives in person or Zoom, and P-014 says only the full Board adopts.
units.problem: Low; a citation gap, not a factual error. None of the cited passages supports the new timing clause 'before it adopts the budget'. That rests on P-005 (proposal due Nov 15, then adoption by the second regular January meeting), which isn't cited. The clause is almost certainly true. 'It' also refers back to a possessive ('Board of Commissioners' public comment').
units.suggested_fix: Cite [P-036, P-039, P-067, P-005, P-014], and write 'before the Board adopts the budget'.

framing_issues.text: What the jail, courts, prosecutors and public defense get for 2027
framing_issues.issue: Undefined term. 'Public defense' is less familiar to a new reader than 'public defender' and could be misread as policing or public safety. Its definition comes later on the tab (L51), worded as 'public defender's office', so the reader may not connect the two. If the line's word budget allows, use 'public defenders (lawyers for people who can't pay)'.

framing_issues.text: The solicitor-general's office prosecutes misdemeanors. ... The district attorney prosecutes serious crimes, called felonies.
framing_issues.issue: Undefined term. The new district attorney definition explains 'felonies', but 'misdemeanors', in the unchanged solicitor-general sentence earlier on the same line, is still undefined jargon. The reader meets it before the felony contrast that would explain it. Suggest '...prosecutes less serious crimes, called misdemeanors', or put the district attorney sentence first.

framing_issues.text: Resolution 26-0460, which Commissioner Bob Ellis sponsored, says ...
framing_issues.issue: Unequal attribution between the two process lines. L132 now attributes the words to the document ('Resolution 26-0460 ... says'), but the unchanged L133 makes Option C's title Barrett's own purpose ('Barrett ... proposed it "to ensure transparency ..."'). L132 also names only Ellis, though P-016/P-017 list Vice Chair Abdur-Rahman as co-sponsor. Suggest making L133 match: 'Option C, which Commissioner Dana Barrett sponsored, says it aims "to ensure transparency and informed decision-making ..."'.

framing_issues.text: The 2026 plan left savings about $2.8 million above the least the county must keep.
framing_issues.issue: Tense. Past-tense 'left' presents the adopted plan's projected year-end balance as an outcome; 2026 hadn't closed by Nov 8, 2026. L108 and L242 use 'leaves'.

framing_issues.text: The six are the sheriff, district attorney, solicitor-general, court clerk, probate judge and public defender.
framing_issues.issue: Undefined term. The district attorney, solicitor-general, court clerk and public defender get new definitions, but 'probate judge', which is jargon at grade 6 to 8, gets none on this tab; only the Summary tab (L78) explains the probate court. A cited definition is available: 'The probate court handles estates, guardianships, marriage licenses and weapons carry licenses, among other services. [P-087]'.

framing_issues.text: ...court clerk, probate judge and public defender. [P-069, P-070]
framing_issues.issue: Undefined term, same as L143: 'probate judge' isn't defined on this tab while the other offices are. A cited definition is available from P-087.

framing_issues.text: No 2027 source we archived argued against more money for those offices.
framing_issues.issue: Vague reference created by the inserted definitions. Three sentences now sit between 'those offices' and its antecedent ('six justice offices'), and the nearest noun is 'the public defender's office', so a reader could take it to mean only the offices just defined. Suggest 'for the six offices'.

framing_issues.text: When that proposal was written, consent decree costs were ...
framing_issues.issue: Vague reference. 'That proposal' has no antecedent in this field; the sentences before it mention 'the 2026 budget message', not a proposal. Suggest 'When the 2026 proposal was written' or 'When that message was written'.

framing_issues.text: ...public comment, in person or by Zoom, before it adopts the budget.
framing_issues.issue: Vague reference. 'It' points back to a possessive ('Board of Commissioners' public comment'), whose grammatical head is 'public comment'. On a phone-first home item, write 'before the Board adopts the budget'.
